Rashi on Temurah 9b:11:1.hebrew: ואין הקדש שני מוסיף חומש - והיינו הקדש שני, כגון שהומם הראשון וחיללו על אחר, והוי האי אחר הקדש שני. ואם הומם וחיללו, אינו מוסיף עליו חומש. ותמורה נמי הויא הקדש שני:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:11:1.english: And a second consecration does not add a fifth - This is a second consecration: for example, where the first [animal] became blemished and he redeemed it onto another [animal], and this other [animal] became a second consecration. If it [too] became blemished and he redeemed it, he does not add a fifth to it. And a substitute [animal] (temurah) is also considered a second consecration.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:13:1.hebrew: הפריש אשם להתכפר בו כו' - כדלעיל, דהוו להו שני גופים ושתי קדושות, מהו:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:13:1.english: He designated a guilt offering to achieve atonement with it, etc. - As above, that there are here two bodies [i.e., two animals] and two sanctities — what is [the halakha]?

Rashi on Temurah 9b:14:1.hebrew: מאי קא מיבעיא ליה - לרבי אבין. דסלקא אדעתין דבעיא דר' אבין לאו שני גופין ושתי קדושות בעי, אלא בתרי מילי פליג מילתיה. דקמייתא הוו שני גופין וקדושה אחת, ואידך נתכפר באשם אחר — כלומר, שלא הומם הראשון אלא שאבד, ונתכפר באחר, ונמצא זה, וניתק לעולה — דהוו להו שתי קדושות וגוף אחד, מהו? הלכך פריך אביי: הי מינייהו עיקר בעיא דר' אבין? ליבעי להדיא, ולישמע אידך מינה:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:14:1.english: What is the dilemma he is raising? - Of Rabbi Avin. For it entered our mind that Rabbi Avin's dilemma does not ask about two bodies and two sanctities, but rather he divides his matter into two cases. In the first case, there are two bodies and one sanctity; and in the other, he achieved atonement through a different guilt offering — that is, the first animal did not become blemished but was lost, and he achieved atonement through another, and this one was found and was consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering — so that there are two sanctities and one body: what is the law? Therefore Abaye asks: Which of them is the main dilemma of Rabbi Avin? Let him ask it explicitly, and the other would be understood from it.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:14:2.hebrew: אי שני גופין וקדושה אחת קמיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא נתכפר - באחר, אלא הומם הראשון וחיללו והוסיף עליו חומש. דחומש לא שייך בקדשי מזבח בלא מום, דהא תם לא נפיק לחולין. והומם האי שני, מהו? כלומר, מי אמרינן: כיון דקדושה אחת היא, אינו מוסיף בה חומש אחרינא, או דילמא כיון דב' גופין נינהו, מוסיף בה חומש? וכי אמר ר' יהושע הקדש שני אינו מוסיף ביה חומש, כגון מתפיס בעל מום לבדק הבית וחיללו בבעל מום אחר, דהאי לא מחדש בה מידי. אבל הכא דמתפיס תם בבעל מום, דהאי חזי למזבח, הקדש שני קרינן ביה, דההוא קמא לא חזי אלא לדמי, והאי חזי למזבח, וקדושה חדשה היא:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:14:2.english: If [he is asking about] two bodies and one sanctity, let him ask it in [a case where] he did not achieve atonement - with another [guilt offering]; rather, the first [animal] was blemished, and he redeemed it and added a fifth to it. (For a fifth does not apply to sacrificial consecrated animals without a blemish, since an unblemished animal cannot go out to ordinary status.) And this second [animal] was blemished — what is the law? That is to say, do we say: Since it is one sanctity, he does not add another fifth for it? Or perhaps, since they are two bodies, he does add a fifth for it? And when Rabbi Yehoshua said that a second consecration does not add a fifth, [that applies to] a case such as one who consecrates a blemished animal for Temple maintenance and redeems it with another blemished animal, since this does not innovate anything in it. But here, where he consecrates an unblemished animal with a blemished one — since this [unblemished one] is fit for the altar — we call it a "second consecration," because that first one was fit only for its value, whereas this one is fit for the altar, and it is a new sanctity.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:15:1.hebrew: אי שתי קדושות וגוף אחד מיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא הומם - קודם שאבד, אלא אבד והפריש אחרת ונתכפר בו, ונמצא הראשון וניתק לעולה, מהו? מי אמרינן הקדש שני הוא, שהרי נתכפר באחר וזה טפל לו, ואם הומם ובא לחללו לא יוסיף עליו חומש, או דלמא כיון דשתי קדושות נינהו ה"ל הקדש ראשון לענין זה ומוסיף חומש:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:15:1.english: If [he is asking] about two sanctities and one body, let him raise the question even without its having become blemished - [that is, the dilemma could be raised in a case where the animal was not blemished] before it was lost, but rather it was lost, and [the owner] set aside another [animal] and atoned with it, and then the first was found and was consigned to be a burnt offering. What is the law? Do we say that it is the second consecration [that counts as the primary one], since [the owner] already atoned with the other, and this [first animal] is secondary to it, so that if it became blemished and he comes to redeem it, he does not add a fifth to it? Or perhaps, since they are two sanctities, the first consecration is considered [a consecration] with regard to this matter, and he adds a fifth:

Rashi on Temurah 9b:16:1.hebrew: חדא מגו חדא - כלומר, סיפא דבעייא דרבי אבין, ארישא דמילתא קאי, ולאו מילתא אחריתי היא, אלא שני גופין ושתי קדושות בעי:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:16:1.english: One from [the other] - That is to say, the latter part of Rabbi Avin's dilemma refers back to the first part of the matter, and it is not a different matter; rather, he is inquiring about [the case of] two bodies and two sanctities.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:16:2.hebrew: ואם תמצא לומר קאמר - אם תמצא לומר, היינו חדא מגו חדא:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:16:2.english: "And if you find [it] to say" he is saying - "If you find [it] to say" is the same as [the dilemma of] one [dilemma] arising out of another.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:16:3.hebrew: מהו - מי אמרי', כיון דשני גופין ושתי קדושות נינהו, לא מיקרי הקדש שני ומוסיף חומש, דהא בהא קדושה והאי גופא לא אתוסף חומשו? או דלמא סוף סוף מכח קמא אתא (מעיקרא) והקדש שני הוא לגבי חומש? לישנא אחרינא: ירושלמי, וכלישנא בתרא דלעיל דבעיא דרבי אבין גבי תמורה, גרסי' לה נמי הכא, ופירושי מפרש:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:16:3.english: What is [the halakha]? - Do we say that since they are two bodies and two sanctities, it is not called a "second consecration" that requires adding a fifth, because this sanctity is in one animal and in this body its fifth was not added? Or perhaps, after all, it came from the force of the first (originally), and it is a second consecration with respect to the fifth? Another version: The reading of the Yerushalmi, and like the latter version above, is that the dilemma of Rabbi Avin concerning temura is also read here, and it explains it accordingly.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:1:1.english: And it became blemished - the first [guilt offering].

Rashi on Temurah 9b:1:2.hebrew: וחיללו על אחר ונתכפר באשם אחר - אחר שאבד אשם שני, זה שחילל הראשון עליו, ונתכפר באחר, ואח"כ נמצא זה:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:1:2.english: And he desacralized it onto another, and atoned with another guilt offering - After the second guilt offering was lost — the one onto which he desacralized the first — and he atoned with another [animal], and afterward this [second one] was found.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:1:3.hebrew: וניתק לעולה - דאשם שכיפרו בעליו באחר, סתמיה לשם עולת נדבת צבור קאי, דהיינו מן המותרות, דמדרש יהוידע הכהן בפ' ולד חטאת (לקמן תמורה דף כג:):
Rashi on Temurah 9b:1:3.english: And it was consigned to a burnt offering - For a guilt offering whose owners achieved atonement through another, [the animal] by default stands for the sake of a communal voluntary burnt offering, namely from the surplus funds, [as derived] from the exposition of Jehoiada the Priest, in the chapter [entitled] Veled Chatat (below, Temurah 23b).

Rashi on Temurah 9b:1:4.hebrew: מהו שימירו בו - מי אמרינן כיון דמכח קמא אתא, אין ממירין בו, דהא המיר בראשון? או דלמא כיון דגופא אחרינא הוא, וקדושה אחריתי היא — דכי המיר בקמא הוה אשם, והאי הוה עולה — הלכך ממירין:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:1:4.english: What is [the law] that he can substitute for it? - Do we say: since it comes by virtue of the first [animal], one may not substitute for it, for he already effected a substitution for the first one? Or perhaps, since it is a different body and it is a different sanctity — for when he substituted for the first it was a guilt offering, and this one is a burnt offering — therefore one may substitute for it.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:2:1.hebrew: אי שני גופין וקדושה אחת מיבעיא ליה - דמי אמרינן כיון דגופא אחרינא הוה, מימר; או דלמא כיון דקדושה אחת היא, לא מימר:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:2:1.english: If [it is] two bodies and one sanctity, [why] is he asking - Do we say that since it is a different body, [the substitution] takes effect (mimar)? Or perhaps, since it is one sanctity, [the substitution] does not take effect:

Rashi on Temurah 9b:2:2.hebrew: אי הכי מיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא נתכפר - דהכי איבעי ליה למימר: הפריש אשם להתכפר בו, והמיר בו, והומם הראשון, וחיללו על אחר — מהו שימיר בזה האחר? כיון דגופא אחרינא הוא — מימר, או דלמא כיון דמכח קמא אתא, וחדא קדושה דקמא הוה אשם והאי נמי אשם — לא מימר? ולמה לי למימר שהוא נתכפר באחר:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:2:2.english: If so, [why] is he asking this? Let him ask it in a case where he had not achieved atonement - For this is how he should have phrased it: [If someone] set aside a guilt offering to achieve atonement with it, and then substituted for it, and the first [animal] became blemished and he redeemed it for another [animal] — what is the law as to whether he can substitute with this other [animal]? Since it is a different body, he can substitute; or perhaps, since it came by the power of the first, and the first one's single sanctity was that of a guilt offering and this one too is a guilt offering, he cannot substitute? So why did he need to say [that the owner] had achieved atonement with another [animal]?

Rashi on Temurah 9b:4:1.hebrew: חדא מגו חדא - כלומר, "אם תמצא לומר" קאמר, וחדא בעיא היא. והכי קאמר: הפריש אשם, והמיר בו, והומם, וחיללו — דהוה ליה האי גוף שני וקדושה אחת — מהו?:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:4:1.english: One from [within] the other - That is, he says "if you should say," and it is [really] one question. And this is what he is saying: If one set aside a guilt-offering and substituted [another animal] for it, and [the original] became blemished and he redeemed it, so that this [substituted animal] is a second body and one sanctity — what is the law?

Rashi on Temurah 9b:4:2.hebrew: ואם תימצי לומר - הכא, כיון דקדושה אחת היא, אינו מימר (משום דבההיא קדושה) איתמר בה תמורה, ואינו מימר בה פעם אחרת:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:4:2.english: And if you say - Here, since it is one sanctity, [the second animal] does not effect substitution (because that sanctity) [substitution] has [already] been stated regarding it, and it does not effect substitution regarding it another time.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:4:3.hebrew: שני גופין ושתי קדושות מהו - כגון אבד, והפריש אחר תחתיו, ונמצא הראשון, ועתה יש שניהם, שני זה מתכפר באחר, ושני ניתק לעולה כשנמצא. מהו? כיון דהשתא שני הוא וקדושה אחרת היא, מימר, או דלמא סוף סוף מכח קמא אתא, ואינו מימר? בלישנא אחרינא, ירושלמי גרסי' לה, ותרתי קבעי: הפריש אשם והמיר בו, והומם, וחיללו על אחר, מהו שימיר בו? דהוי ליה שני גופין וקדושה אחת, ומספקא ליה כדפרישית בלישנא דלעיל. או שלא הומם, אלא (אם) נתכפר באחר, וניתק זה לעולה כשנמצא, והוה ליה שתי קדושות וגוף אחד, מהו שימיר? ופירושא כדפרישית:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:4:3.english: Two bodies and two sanctities, what is the law? - For example, [an offering] was lost, [and he set aside another in its place, and then the first was found, so that now both exist]; the second one atones through another [offering], and the second one is sent to graze until it becomes blemished and is offered as a burnt offering when [the first] is found. What is the law? Since now it is a second [animal] and it is a different sanctity, does it effect substitution, or perhaps, after all, it came by the power of the first, and it does not effect substitution? In another version — we read it in the Jerusalem Talmud — and he asks two [questions]: If one set aside a guilt offering and substituted for it, and it became blemished, and he redeemed it on another [animal], what is the law as to whether [the other] can effect substitution? For this is two bodies and one sanctity, and he is uncertain about it, as I explained in the earlier version. Or [the case is] that it did not become blemished, but (if) it atoned through another [offering], and this one was sent to graze until it became blemished and is offered as a burnt offering when [it] is found, so that it has two sanctities and one body; what is the law as to whether it effects substitution? And the explanation is as I explained.

Rashi on Temurah 9b:7:1.hebrew: אמר (ליה) אביי הדין קמיבעיא - אי זו מהן הויא עיקר שאלתו, אי קדושה אחרת באותו הגוף כו' כדפרישית, דהיינו גוף אחד ושתי קדושות, לא ניבעי הומם וחיללו כו'. ורבי אבין, חדא מגו חדא קא מיבעיא ליה, ואת"ל קאמר. והשתא להאי לישנא לא בעי מידי משני גופים ושתי קדושות, אלא ה"ק: אם תימצי לומר גוף אחד באותה קדושה כו'. ולהאי לישנא חשיב שני גופין וקדושה אחת חדא טפי משתי קדושות וגוף אחד:
Rashi on Temurah 9b:7:1.english: Abaye said (to him): Which is the one he is asking about? - Which of them is the main point of his question? If [it is] another sanctity in the same body, etc., as I explained, that is, one body and two sanctities, he should not ask [about the case where] it became blemished and he desacralized it, etc. But Rabbi Avin [holds that] he is asking one question from within the other, and [the second case] is stated as an "if you say." And now, according to this version, he does not ask anything at all about two bodies and two sanctities; rather, this is what he is saying: If you say [that the case of] one body with the same sanctity, etc. And according to this version, he considers two bodies and one sanctity to be one [case] more [likely to be a question] than two sanctities and one body.
